## Proposition: exact dominance reduction of the existential suffix observer

For fixed remaining depth d, C_d is the inherited R247/R303 optimistic capacity predicate. By R303, C_d is downward hereditary on original germ sets. A split L=(X,Y) dominates M=(A,B) for this existential predicate if X subset A and Y subset B, up to swapping the branches. For any state S, intersection preserves both inclusions. Thus if M makes both C_{d-1} child predicates true, L also makes both true. The child capacity filter is hereditary for the same reason. If both splits are available in the current library, deleting M while retaining L preserves the existential value. The converse follows because the retained library is a sublibrary. The terminal capacity and optimistic acceptance tests do not change. By induction in d, replacing the full library by a sublibrary containing a retained dominator for every removed split preserves C_d on every germ subset. This proof uses the actual two complete child masks, not their tag counts. A zero germ in L may become nonzero in M; the dominance is directed, not an equality of observations. The saturated library is unchanged, and every dominator is one of its retained wall splits; hence both libraries' applicability is respected. This is only a decision-preserving reduction of the specified existential necessary predicate, not a proof of physical equivalence of directions or of exact tree realizability. Original split identities and all removed-to-retained mappings are recoverable from frozen input. A path-dependent or zero-branch-dependent stronger predicate would require a fresh proof.
